name: Reverse Box Turn (backward half)
notes: Owner's description (2026-11-16): the Box Turn with everything reversed. Follows Reverse Box Turn (forward half); the lead starts back on the right foot, side on the left, close the right, turning a quarter to the left. The mirror image of Box Turn (backward half), with the same sizes (0.5 back, then the left foot lands 0.4 beyond the right in the turned frame, measured from the facing before the turn as 0.9 back and 0.2 right), the whole quarter turn on count 2, the feet closing on 3 and no rise. Called the Left Box Turn in the American syllabus. The lead goes back on step 2, so the couple turns round him (the default turning centre). Turn timing from the book (2026-11-17, a box-step study card: the partner going forward turns 1/8 between 1 and 2 and 1/8 between 2 and 3; the partner going back turns 1/4 between 1 and 2, "body turns less", and the body completes the turn on 3): the bodies turn 1/8 left on count 2 and 1/8 on the close, and the lead, going back on the inside of the turn, points the foot a further 1/8 on count 2 (`pointing`), so his feet make the whole quarter between 1 and 2. The close's turn is carried back into count 2's foot placement, so the feet land exactly where they did with the whole quarter on count 2.
